findings.title: The minimum token schema strips expiry fields and refresh tokens
findings.body: These computed keys are stringified Zod schema objects, not wildcards for arbitrary response properties; both expressions resolve to the same literal property name, so the second also overwrites the first. Zod therefore strips real fields such as `expiry_date` and `expires_in` from the parsed response. The function then substitutes the literal `"refresh_token"` when the real refresh token was stripped or absent. Token refreshes can consequently save credentials without a valid expiry or refresh token, causing repeated refreshes or permanently breaking future refreshes.

findings.title: The sync branch returns a Fetch Response to callers expecting parsed token data
findings.body: When credential syncing is enabled, this returns the raw `Response` from `fetch`, whereas several callers treat the result as parsed data or an Axios response. For example, Bigin and Zoho CRM read `tokenInfo.data`, and HubSpot reads token fields directly from the returned value; with the sync branch active those fields are undefined, so token persistence and authentication fail. Parse the endpoint response into the same shape each caller expects, or give the helper a consistent return contract.

findings.title: Salesforce constructs its connection with the expired tokens
findings.body: The code refreshes the Salesforce access token and saves the refreshed response, but constructs the connection using `credentialKey.instance_url` and `credentialKey.access_token` from the original credential. If that access token was expired, the new connection still uses it and Salesforce API calls fail despite the successful refresh. Build the connection from the refreshed token response.

findings.title: Salesforce token refresh bypasses the credential sync endpoint
findings.body: This refresh path calls Salesforce directly instead of using `refreshOAuthTokens`, so configuring `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` has no effect for Salesforce credentials. Self-hosters who rely on their app store as the source of truth will still refresh Salesforce credentials using Cal.com's provider credentials, contrary to the syncing behavior added for the other integrations.

findings.title: Bigin sends a credential ID as the remote user ID
findings.body: The third argument is used by `refreshOAuthTokens` as `calcomUserId` in the sync request, but this call passes `credentialId`, not the credential owner's `userId`. The self-hosted app store therefore receives a credential record ID where it expects a user ID and cannot reliably refresh the correct user's token. Pass `credential.userId`.

findings.title: Concurrent sync requests can create duplicate credentials
findings.body: The handler performs a `findFirst` followed by a separate `create` when no credential is found. Two concurrent webhook deliveries for the same user and app can both observe no row and create duplicates; subsequent `findFirst` calls may then update an arbitrary duplicate. Make this operation atomic, for example with an appropriate unique constraint and upsert or a transaction that prevents duplicate creation.
